clue.text: Pledges with wines

definitions.meaning: to pledge something is to pawn it, to put it in hock
German white wines from the Rhine region, named after the town of Hochheim

explanation.definitionFit: To pawn goods is to hock them, and hock is the British name for Rhine wine, so the plural fits both senses.

clue.text: Hydrangea is another variety of it

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so these letters take a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that the hydrangea is just another variety of some familiar plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges IS ANOTHER; 'it' is the link pointing at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hortensia is an old name for the garden hydrangea, especially the mophead kind.

clue.text: Credit America with party-piece valued by Portuguese

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts
USA, the United States of America
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone praises America for a party piece much admired in Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party-piece' looks like one phrase, but the hyphen splits it: 'party' gives DO and 'piece' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The crusado was an old Portuguese coin, a piece of money valued in Portugal.

clue.text: Team in division?

definitions.meaning: a team in sport
a ... is one of the parts something is divided into, as in either ... of a line

explanation.definitionFit: A football eleven is a side, and a partition separates two sides, each being one part of the split.

clue.text: Supporters of FA trophy winners, leaderless

indicators.note: without a leader means the first letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: the FA Cup is English football's main knockout trophy
the winners of a cup are its holders

explanation.surface: Fans of the club that has just won the FA Cup find themselves without a captain.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA Cup is English football's main knockout trophy; 'leaderless' drops the C from CUP HOLDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who uphold something are its backers, people who keep it standing.

clue.text: The Student Prince, say, as a very old fellow

definitions.meaning: the hero of the operetta The Student Prince studies at Heidelberg University, so he is a man of that town
a fossil human species known from a jaw found near Heidelberg, hundreds of thousands of years old

explanation.definitionFit: Sigmund Romberg's operetta prince is a student at Heidelberg, and an early human species was named for a jawbone found nearby.

clue.text: American city's hard hit

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, and the possessive adds the S
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A US city has been badly struck by some disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash is to strike, as with a whip, so it is a synonym for hit.

clue.text: To embrace partner requires energy initially

indicators.note: at the start means the energy letter goes before the partner word

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
a spouse is a marriage partner

explanation.surface: Hugging one's other half takes a bit of effort first.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to adopt or take it up, a figurative embrace.

clue.text: Withered edges of lakeside grass

indicators.note: something withered is shrivelled out of shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The grass by the lake has dried and browned at the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grassy plant that grows in wet ground at the water's edge.

clue.text: Slice of bread at university assembly

parts.note: a round is a slice of bread, or a sandwich made from two
a student who is up is in residence at university

explanation.surface: A sandwich being served to a university gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at university is British usage, especially for Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A round-up gathers people or cattle together into one assembly.

clue.text: Chair for shoppers is brought out

indicators.note: to bring out is to draw these letters out into a new form

explanation.surface: A seat is put out on the shop floor for tired shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: A university chair is a professor's post, the title held by its holder.

clue.text: Flat spin, perhaps, after one? I would bring up the rear!

indicators.note: after one means the reworked word follows the numeral

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: A dull bit of spin follows someone, who then cheerfully offers to come last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SPIN into NSIP; 'bring up the rear' simply places ID at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat food or prose lacks taste or interest, which is to be insipid.

clue.text: Dash from the lane

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone rushes out from the lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash means verve or flair, the stylish energy also called panache.

clue.text: Arrange insurance for this fielder

definitions.meaning: to take out a policy is to get protection against loss
a cricket fielding position on the off side, square of the batsman

explanation.definitionFit: An insurer provides protection for a risk, and a fielding post in cricket shares the same word.

clue.text: Clio is one to speculate

definitions.meaning: Clio is the Greek goddess of history, one of the nine daughters of Zeus who inspire the arts
to ponder or meditate

explanation.definitionFit: Clio belongs to the nine inspiring goddesses, and to ponder or reflect is a verb sense of the same word.

clue.text: Worked diligently to produce soft, Schubert song

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
a Lied is a German art song, of which Schubert wrote hundreds

explanation.surface: A composer laboured to write a quiet Schubert song.
explanation.definitionFit: To ply a trade is to work at it steadily, so the past tense means laboured hard.

clue.text: Eat small amounts-it makes sense

definitions.meaning: to try a little of a dish
one of the five senses, the one on the tongue

explanation.definitionFit: To sample food is to try a little, and the sense of flavour is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Bear sword here when receiving accolade?

parts.note: to shoulder a burden is to bear it
a blade is a sword

explanation.surface: A knight-to-be is told to carry a sword here while being honoured.
explanation.walkthrough: The accolade is the tap of a sword on the shoulder that confers a knighthood, so the definition points to where the blade touches.
explanation.definitionFit: In a knighting ceremony the sword is laid upon the upper back near the arm, the flat bone there.

clue.text: Room in Hull, we hear, making no charge for accommodation?

definitions.meaning: Hull the city sounds like a ship's hull; the height of a ship's side above the waterline
offering lodging and meals at no cost, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Freeboard is the clearance between waterline and deck of a ship, and free board means meals and lodging supplied gratis.

clue.text: Coins buried out-rarest ever, it turns out

indicators.note: turns out signals these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A hoard of buried coins proves to be the rarest find ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure trove is valuables, especially coins or gold, found hidden in the ground with no known owner.

clue.text: Set out to mimic

definitions.meaning: to leave the ground or depart
to impersonate someone for comic effect

explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft departs by leaving the runway, and a comedian does an impression by parodying someone.

clue.text: Offence to line new route with silver?

indicators.note: to line is to sit inside something, so the silver goes within the reworked letters
new suggests the word route is made over in a fresh order

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Locals are offended by a plan to edge a new road with silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to line' looks like drawing a line, but here silver lining the road means it sits inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking offence and feeling indignation are both named by this word.

clue.text: Solid fuel approved in church

indicators.note: in places the approval letters inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OK means approved

explanation.surface: A church has been given the nod to heat itself with solid fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is the carbon-rich residue of coal, burned as smokeless fuel.

clue.text: Chests of people attending hospital

definitions.meaning: boxes or trunks for packing things
patients a doctor treats

explanation.definitionFit: Packing crates are cases, and patients on a ward are spoken of as cases.

clue.text: Fellow takes seat of dowdy woman

parts.note: the seat is the buttocks, the rump

explanation.surface: A man sits down on the bottom of an unfashionable lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A frump is a drably dressed, unfashionable woman.

clue.text: Run through tar on street

indicators.note: in an across clue, X on Y puts X after Y

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, as is an AB, an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor is stabbed in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone through is to pierce them with a blade.

clue.text: Packaged, you say, to be transported

indicators.note: you say signals the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: something packaged has been put in wrapping

explanation.surface: Someone is told their parcel will be wrapped and sent off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone transported with joy is enraptured, carried away in delight.

clue.text: Report the fringe

definitions.meaning: a loud explosive noise, like a gun's report
hair cut straight across the forehead, chiefly American usage

explanation.definitionFit: A gunshot's loud noise is called a report, and in America hair cut across the forehead is known by the same word.

clue.text: Put up with Thomas Twist?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Put up with Thomas Twist?' (7): THOMAS gives six letters and nothing supplies the C of STOMACH; no scan, and a search of the text finds no fuller version

clue.text: A river once more backs up and falls

indicators.note: backs means turns back to front, so the run of pieces reads in the other direction

parts.note: again means once more

explanation.surface: A river rises again, then cascades down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs up' turns A R AGAIN round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterfalls on the US-Canada border take this name.

clue.text: Peter, workin 'at keyboard, needs a security device

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
working at a keyboard is typing, and the dropped g is shown by the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man named Peter, busy typing, needs some protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a name, but in old thieves' slang a peter is a safe; the dropped-g spelling of 'workin' tells you to clip TYPING to TYPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin with a guarded point is a small fastening device that keeps clothing secure.

clue.text: Longing for good long grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass that grows in wet places

explanation.surface: Someone yearns for nice tall grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an excessive longing for wealth or food.
